description: Grade 5 example: name an interval under a key signature (F# major, alto clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of F# major is shown. Name the interval between these two notes (number and quality).

music.textAlternative: Two notes in F♯ major (six sharps) in the alto clef: G♯3 and B3. The G♯ comes from the key signature. Both notes are minims.

hints: Apply the key signature to both notes before you count.
Count the letter names for the number, then compare with the major scale on the lower note for the quality.

feedback.correct: Correct. F♯ major has six sharps (F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯ A♯ E♯), so the G is G♯. G♯ to B is a minor 3rd; G♮ to B would be a major 3rd.

mistakes.ignored-key-signature: Read the notes as bare letters? F♯ major has six sharps (F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯ A♯ E♯), so the G is G♯. G♯ to B is a minor 3rd; G♮ to B would be a major 3rd.
mistakes.counted-one-end-only: Count both notes: the lower note is 1, then every letter name up to and including the upper note.
mistakes.quality-from-wrong-key: Judge the quality against the major scale of the lower note, using the sharps or flats actually sounding.

feedback.fallback: The answer is a minor 3. F♯ major has six sharps (F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯ A♯ E♯), so the G is G♯. G♯ to B is a minor 3rd; G♮ to B would be a major 3rd.
